answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must contact MSHA immediately, and within 15 minutes, once it knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes of knowing or having reason to know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: This applies to an accident involving a death of an individual at the mine.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. The chunk raises this percentage only where methane is present.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The percentage is increased only where methane is present in a ventilating current.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Under 30 CFR 75.1714, the operator must make available to each underground miner an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. The drills must be held for each shift, at some time other than a shift change.

claims.text: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold evacuation drills at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety

claims.text: The drills must be held for each shift, at some time other than a shift change.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. Approximately 8 of those hours must be given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties, and approximately 8 hours of it must be given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The chunks don't state the permissible exposure level as an 8-hour average figure. They say a noise dose uses a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate. The action level is a TWA8 of 85 dBA and the dual hearing protection level is a TWA8 of 105 dBA. The PEL itself is not given as a TWA8 number here.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. This appears in both 30 CFR 56.9300 (surface metal and nonmetal mines) and 57.9300 (underground metal and nonmetal mines).

claims.text: Under 56.9300, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Under 57.9300, the same height requirement applies: at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The chunks don't answer this question. They cover MSHA mining rules (engine exhaust systems, shaft deepening protection, miner training, and equipment definitions). None of them mention OSHA construction trench requirements or the depth at which a protective system is required.
